children.translated_text: Having bowed to the supreme lord and then to the sage <s>Bharadvāja</s>,
listen, O well-vowed ones, to the knowledge that came in succession from <s>Hara</s> to <s>Indra</s>.
In the holy hermitage of <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, brahmins beginning with <s>Bharadvāja</s>,
having installed <s>Śiva</s>, practiced austerity with their minds intent on him alone.

children.text: atha tān bhāvitān matvā kadācit tridaśādhipaḥ
children.translated_text: Then once, thinking them to be inwardly purified, the lord of the thirty gods
came himself to that hermitage, wearing the guise of an ascetic.

children.text: sa taiḥ sampūjitaḥ pṛṣṭvā tāṃś ca sarvān anāmayam
children.translated_text: Honored by them, he asked all of them about their well-being,
and said: "Why is the <s>dharma</s> prescribed by injunction not being followed?"

children.text: ta ūcur nanv ayaṃ dharmaś codanāvihito mune
children.translated_text: They said: "Surely this is precisely the <s>dharma</s> prescribed by injunction, O sage:
the means of worshiping the deity through austerity for the accomplishment of one's desired aim.

children.text: vede 'sti saṃhitā raudrī vācyā rudraś ca devatā
children.translated_text: In the Veda there is a <s>Raudrī Saṃhitā</s>; its speaker is <s>Rudra</s>, and <s>Rudra</s> is the deity.
Even for making his presence manifest in this rite, a ritual procedure belonging to the kalpa is prescribed."

children.text: ity ukte 'pi paraṃ bhāvaṃ jijñāsuḥ prahasan prabhuḥ
children.translated_text: Although this was said, the lord, wishing to know their highest disposition, laughed

children.text: tān āha mithyā jñānaṃ vaḥ śabdamātraṃ hi devatā ||
children.translated_text: and said to them: "Your knowledge is false, for the deity is merely a word.
If she were something other than a word, when worshipers are at the same time in different places,

children.text: na sā prayāti sāṃnidhyaṃ mūrtatvād asmadādivat ||
children.translated_text: she would not come into presence there, because she would be embodied, like us and others.

children.text: na ca tatsādhakaṃ kiṃcit pramāṇaṃ bhāty abādhitam
children.translated_text: And no means of knowledge, uncontradicted and proving that, appears at all.

children.text: vākyaṃ tad anyathāsiddhaṃ lokavādāḥ kva sādhavaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The scriptural sentence can be established otherwise; how could common sayings be valid authorities?"
Though driven against by the shoreline-waves of speech denying the Lord,
their mountain of understanding did not move before <s>Śakra</s>, because of the weight of its substance, like an ocean.
"Never is the form of a deity like the bodies of ourselves and others.
It is endowed with extraordinary lordly power; therefore this example is not applicable.

children.text: athāstv evaṃ ghaṭe nyāyaḥ śabdatvād indraśabdavat
children.translated_text: Now suppose this reasoning applies to a pot: because it is a word, like the word 'Indra'.
The word 'pot' does not take up water, and the word 'moon' does not shine.
Or let the sentence have another object, denoting <s>Śakra</s> and the rest.
How then would words for action, form, and so on be meaningful?

children.text: pravādo 'py akhilo mithyā samūlatvān na yuktimat
children.translated_text: Nor is every report false on the ground that it has a basis; that is not reasonable.

children.text: sa ced amūlo bhūtānāṃ hatāḥ sarvāḥ pravṛttayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: If it were without basis, all activities of living beings would be destroyed.

children.text: upamanyur haraṃ dṛṣṭvā vimanyur abhavan muniḥ
children.translated_text: The sage <s>Upamanyu</s>, having seen <s>Hara</s>, became free from distress.

children.text: kathaṃ tasya vaco mithyā yasya vaśyaḥ payonidhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: How could the word of him be false, under whose command the ocean of milk stood?
Enclosed by the noose that emitted a row of poisonous flames,

children.text: mocitaḥ patyā dṛṣṭaḥ śveto ghanair janaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Śveta</s> was seen by many people to have been freed by the Lord with a huṃ-call."
Thus, through the connection of the debate, they were delighted by praise of <s>Hara</s>.
Seeing them, their voices choked and faltering with tears, the steadfast one became pleased.

children.text: svaṃ rūpaṃ darśayāmāsa vajrī devaḥ śatakratuḥ
children.translated_text: The god <s>Vajrī</s>, <s>Śatakratu</s>, showed his own form,
like the young sun, praised by the hosts of <s>Maruts</s>.

children.text: te tam ṛgbhir yajurbhiś ca sāmabhiś cāstuvan natāḥ
children.translated_text: Bowing, they praised him with Ṛg-verses, Yajus-formulas, and Sāman-chants.

children.text: so 'bravīd ucyatāṃ kāmo jagatsu pravaro 'pi yaḥ ||
children.translated_text: He said: "Let the wish be spoken, even if it is the highest in the worlds."

children.text: te vavrire śivajñānaṃ śrūyatām iti so 'bravīt
children.translated_text: They chose knowledge of <s>Śiva</s>. "Listen," he said,
"but let there be one questioner for me, approved by all the hearers."

children.text: atha teṣāṃ bharadvājo bhagavān agraṇīr abhūt
children.translated_text: Then among them the venerable <s>Bharadvāja</s> became the foremost.
Eloquent and bold, he questioned the one worshiped by the gods according to proper reasoning:

children.text: kathaṃ maheśvarād etad āgataṃ jñānam uttamam
children.translated_text: "How did this supreme knowledge come from <s>Maheśvara</s>?

children.text: kiṃ ca cetasi saṃsthāpya nirmame bhagavān idam ||
children.translated_text: And with what fixed in his mind did the Blessed One fashion this?"
"At the time of creation, for the fulfillment of human aims, <s>Maheśāna</s>
sets forth stainless knowledge, characterized as having five streams.
In the supreme path he sets forth the host of terms belonging to it, and the eight <s>Maheśvaras</s> denoted by those terms,
as well as the mantras, counted as seventy million.
And there is another revealed teaching, exceeding this by eighteen, for those who preside over māyā,
the lords of mantra, whose brilliance is like that of the Lords established on the higher path.

children.text: teṣu vyaktaḥ sa bhagavān idaṃ yogyeṣu siddhaye
children.translated_text: Among them that Blessed One, manifest for the worthy,
reveals this for accomplishment; hence its meaning is also established among others.
This knowledge, uttered by <s>Śiva</s>, by the lords of mantras and by the lords of mantra-lords,
is widely sung as the <s>Kāmika</s>, because it grants desires, and it is very extensive.
Having learned it from them, the husband of <s>Umā</s>, whose flame of the light of vision licked up the tree of <s>Smara</s>,
gave it to me in thousands of verses equal in number to those of <s>Bhava</s>.
There too, leaving aside the extensive treatment, with aphorisms that express the essential meaning,

children.text: vakṣye nirākulaṃ jñānaṃ taduktair eva bhūyasā ||
children.translated_text: I shall set forth unconfused knowledge, mostly in the very terms stated there.
Now <s>Śiva</s>, free from beginningless impurity, maker of all and knower of all,
removes the net of bonds from the soul whose nature has previously been reversed.
The Lord of the world, having gathered the great tantra, with three topics and four sections,
into a single aphorism, then expounded it again in detail.
The birth, maintenance, destruction, concealment, and liberation of the world,

children.text: kṛtyaṃ sakārakaphalaṃ jñeyam asyaitad eva hi ||
children.translated_text: together with the agent and the result, are precisely what is to be known as his activity.
Therefore the maker of the world must exist by his own nature.
If he were established by something lower, there would be infinite regress, or liberation would be without a cause.

children.text: caitanyaṃ dṛkkriyārūpaṃ tad asty ātmani sarvadā
children.translated_text: Consciousness, whose nature is vision and action, always exists in the self,

children.text: sarvataś ca yato muktau śrūyate sarvatomukham ||
children.translated_text: and from every side, because in liberation it is taught to be facing every direction.

children.text: sad apy abhāsamānatvāt tan niruddhaṃ pratīyate
children.translated_text: Although existent, because it does not appear, it is understood to be obstructed.
It is controllable by one whose power is unobscured; for that very reason there is no release without him.
Karma, variegated by coverings, and the product of māyā, fourfold,
are in brief the net of bonds, the categories merely named as such.
Thus, since this triad of realities has been established by the earlier section,
its application will be explained through the sections on conduct, yoga, and ritual action.
The fruit of that application is liberation, with enjoyment also as an incidental result.
By the division into supreme and non-supreme, those two too are divided in many ways.
In doctrines such as Vedānta, Sāṃkhya, and the schools that posit existent and non-existent categories,

children.text: sasādhanā muktir asti ko viśeṣaḥ śivāgame ||
children.translated_text: there is liberation together with its means; what special distinction is there in the <s>Śivāgama</s>?
Because its propounder sees all systems, the collection of realities is not indistinct;

children.text: upāyāḥ saphalās tadvac chaive sarvam idaṃ param ||
children.translated_text: and likewise the means are fruitful. In the Śaiva teaching all this is supreme.
In the Vedāntas there is one self alone, characterized as the manifestation of consciousness and non-consciousness.
This is merely an assertion; on what is certainty based?
If the self there is a means of knowledge, it assumes the status of an object of knowledge;

children.text: yatraitad ubhayaṃ tatra catuṣṭayam api sthitam ||
children.translated_text: and where these two are present, the whole fourfold set is also established.
Thus there would be a loss of non-duality; otherwise there would be absence of proof.
And equality of enjoyment and non-liberation would follow, both of which the advocates of the self do not accept.
Even in Sāṃkhya knowledge there is falsity, because in the effect there is the cognition of the cause,

children.text: akartṛbhāvād bhoktuś ca svātantryād apy acittvataḥ ||
children.translated_text: and because the enjoyer is not an agent, is independent, and is also without consciousness.

children.text: iha sapta padārthāḥ syur jīvājīvāsravās trayaḥ
children.translated_text: Here there are said to be seven categories: soul, non-soul, influx, these three,

children.text: saṃvaro nirjaraś caiva bandhamokṣāv ubhāv api ||
children.translated_text: restraint, wearing away, and also bondage and liberation, both of them.
But all these, marked by the doctrine of conditional predication, are inconclusive because of non-one-sidedness.

children.text: tad eva sat tadevāsad iti kena pramīyate ||
children.translated_text: By what is it established that the very same thing is existent and the very same thing is non-existent?

children.text: sad anyad asad anyac ca tad evaṃ siddhasādhyatā
children.translated_text: The existent is one thing and the non-existent another; thus what is to be proved is already assumed.

children.text: asaj jaghanyaṃ sac chreṣṭham ity api bruvate budhāḥ ||
children.translated_text: The wise also say that the non-existent is inferior and the existent superior.
Both do not remain in one locus merely because of dependence on that.
But if one says that, when that is absent, the existent is still more connected with it,
then, from fear of confusion among their respective actions, they have also declared it to be non-pervasive.
Because there is no knowledge of the relation between the universal and the other, it is insentient.

children.text: yaḥ prāg avyāpakaḥ so 'nte kathamanyādṛśo bhavet
children.translated_text: That which was formerly non-pervasive: how could it later become of another kind?
If it has properties such as expansion, then there follows a succession of faults.
From the knowledge of the six categories, false knowledge ceases;
then attachment and aversion, possessiveness, and the particular qualities connected with them
gradually cease, since they are born from conjunction with the body.

children.text: sā muktir jaḍatārūpā tato muktaḥ śavo na kim ||
children.translated_text: That liberation is a form of inertness. Then why is a liberated person not a corpse?
Because karma and the like, which manifest consciousness, are momentary, again and again
it is manifested only as it arises, and thus others hold it to be momentary.
That is false, because karma has not yet been enjoyed, and because there is memory of past experience.

children.text: sthitir niranvaye nāśe na smṛter nāpi karmaṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: When there is destruction without any continuing substratum, neither memory nor karma can remain.
If what is characterized by destruction disappears, disturbance is not removed even in liberation.

children.text: na cāsty anubhavaḥ kaścid bhavāvasthā varaṃ tataḥ ||
children.translated_text: Nor is there any experience; therefore the state of existence is preferable.
Having resorted to such doctrines of people deluded by ignorance, the dull-minded
desire release, like those who seek fire from a firefly.

children.text: yat kaivalyaṃ puṃsprakṛtyor vivekād yo vā sarvaṃ brahma matvā virāmaḥ
children.translated_text: Whatever isolation arises from the discrimination of <s>puruṣa</s> and <s>prakṛti</s>, or whatever cessation there is from thinking that everything is <s>brahman</s>,

children.text: yā vā kāścin muktayaḥ pāśajanyās tās tāḥ sarvā bhedam āyānti sṛṣṭau ||
children.translated_text: or whatever liberations are produced by bonds, all those come to differentiation at creation.

children.text: śaive siddho bhāti mūrdhnītareṣāṃ muktaḥ sṛṣṭau punar abhyeti nādhaḥ
children.translated_text: In the Śaiva system the perfected liberated one shines above the heads of the others; at creation he does not again go down below.

children.text: viśvān arthān svena viṣṭabhya dhāmnā sarveśānānīśitaḥ sarvadāste ||
children.translated_text: Holding all objects of the universe by his own radiance, he always remains ruling over all and ruled by none.
Now, having perceived the body and other things as entities that possess the property of being effects,
we know by inference that there is a special maker of this.
Whatever is an effect, of whatever kind and extent, its cause is correspondingly such.
It is eternal, because it is not limited by time, and not localized, because of its vast extension.
Because things arise both successively and non-successively, it possesses the power to produce succession and the rest.

children.text: tasyāsti karaṇaṃ yena dṛṣṭā nākaraṇā kṛtiḥ ||
children.translated_text: It has an instrument by which action is seen, for no act is seen to occur without an instrument.
That instrument is to be known as not arriving later, because the effect has existed from beginningless time.

children.text: karaṇaṃ ca na śaktyanyac chaktirnācetanā citaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The instrument is not something other than power, and power belonging to consciousness is not insentient.
Because there is no restriction of objects, it is one in knowledge and likewise in action.
The effect, such as maintenance and birth, is not from a seed, from <s>prakṛti</s>, or from an atom.

children.text: pāriśeṣyān maheśasya muktasya śiva eva saḥ
children.translated_text: By elimination, it belongs to the liberated great Lord; that one is precisely <s>Śiva</s>.
If the relation is not apprehended, a contradiction comes to someone's means of knowledge.
That same objection applies also to another person: smoke is different on a mountain and in a kitchen and so on.

children.text: loke vapuṣmato dṛṣṭaṃ kṛtyaṃ so 'py asmadādivat ||
children.translated_text: In the world action is seen in one who has a body; that Lord too, like us and others, must have one.

children.text: mūlādyasaṃbhavāc chāktaṃ vapur nas tādṛśaṃ prabhoḥ
children.translated_text: Because root and the rest are impossible, the powerful body of the Lord is not like ours.
That body is made of five mantras useful for the five cosmic acts.
With the mantras <s>Īśa</s>, <s>Tatpuruṣa</s>, <s>Aghora</s>, and those born as <s>Vāma</s> and the rest, it has head and other parts.
By the quality that stands above, with which he rules the whole universe,
that is the head, because it occupies the same region as the head; it is not a limb of a physical body.

children.text: tasya tasya tanuryā pūs tasyām uṣati yena saḥ ||
children.translated_text: In whichever body or form he dwells by means of that,
because of protecting and also manifesting that, he has the face called <s>Tatpuruṣa</s>.

children.text: hṛdayaṃ bodhaparyāyaḥ so 'sya ghoraḥ śivo yataḥ ||
children.translated_text: The heart is a synonym for cognition; since that belongs to him, he is the terrible <s>Śiva</s>.
Because appropriation is terrible, the expression 'terrible' is used figuratively.
He is <s>Vāma</s> because he is contrary to the three aims of life, and he is secret by nature.

children.text: vāmaṃ dhāma paraṃ guhyaṃ yasyāsau vāmaguhyakaḥ
children.translated_text: He whose left side is a supreme, hidden abode is <s>Vāmaguhyaka</s>.

children.text: sadyo'ṇūnāṃ mūrtayaḥ sambhavanti yasyecchātas tena sadyo'bhidhānaḥ
children.translated_text: Because, by his will, the forms of the souls immediately come into being, he has the name <s>Sadya</s>.

children.text: sadyo mūrtīryogināṃ vā vidhatte sadyomūrtiḥ kṛtyaśaighryān na mūrteḥ ||
children.translated_text: Or he immediately establishes forms for yogins; he is <s>Sadyomūrti</s> because his action is swift, not because of an ordinary form.

children.text: itthaṃ śaktiḥ kurvatī dehakṛtyaṃ dehābhāvāducyate dehaśabdaiḥ
children.translated_text: Thus, although the power performs the functions of a body, because there is no physical body it is expressed by words for body.

children.text: tasyā bhedā ye 'pi vāmādayaḥ syuste 'pi proktāḥ kṛtyabhedena sadbhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: And whatever divisions of that power are <s>Vāma</s> and the others, those too are taught by the learned according to difference of function.
He, having such a form, by this instrument of unstruck power,
always performs the action whenever it is fitting.
There, at the beginning, he makes an octad of the worthy isolated atoms,
joined with the powers beginning with <s>Vāmā</s> and furnished with seventy million attendants.
Among them are <s>Ananta</s>, <s>Sūkṣma</s>, and also <s>Śivottama</s>,
<s>Ekanetra</s> and <s>Ekarudra</s>, and <s>Trimūrti</s>, of immeasurable splendor,
<s>Śrīkaṇṭha</s> and <s>Śikhaṇḍī</s>, the lords of the lord of kings.
Because they have only slightly failed to attain full yoga, they are to be employed by the supreme Lord.
Even though they possess omniscience and the rest, they are employable because of a portion of impurity.

children.text: parasparaṃ viśiṣyante mantrāś caivam adhaḥ sthitāḥ ||
children.translated_text: And in this same way the mantras situated below are distinguished from one another.
And they, impelled by the manifest <s>Śiva</s>-power of the lords of mantra,

children.text: kurvantyanugrahaṃ puṃsāṃ yadā yeṣāṃ sa yujyate ||
children.translated_text: bestow grace upon beings whenever that grace is suited to them.
That purpose, dependent on the body of the officiant, throughout the whole path,
having exercised authority until the end of maintenance, enters <s>Śiva</s> together with its lord.
Another, without a substratum, below the transformation of primordial matter,
having exercised the authority desired by the Lord, departs when its own path is withdrawn.
Then, manifested by <s>Ananta</s> and the others, from the bound state of the lords,
he makes one hundred and eighteen whose bodies begin with <s>kalā</s> and the other principles.
Entering even them, the Blessed One appoints the world-rulers, still touched by impurity,
from whom all this proceeds and whose power is bound by karma,
the promulgators of the scriptures for bound souls, and the bound souls who follow them,
furnished with the instruments for what they must accomplish and fixed within the limit of time and place.
In the period of maintenance, pervading these along with their instruments by his own brilliance,
unperceived by the beings, he yokes them for the accomplishment of his own purpose.
Drawing in the means of enjoyment and making it rest in its cause,
and pervading that too together with the self, he remains for repose.
For he is the benefactor of all beings, of those subject to becoming and wearied by becoming.
Having reached the end of sleep, he proceeds again as before.

children.text: svāpe'pyāste bodhayan bodhayogyān rodhyān rundhan pācayankarmikarma
children.translated_text: Even in sleep he remains, awakening those fit for awakening, restraining those to be restrained, and ripening the karmic karma,

children.text: māyāśaktīr vyaktiyogyāḥ prakurvan paśyansarvaṃ yadyathā vastujātam ||
children.translated_text: making the powers of <s>māyā</s> fit for manifestation and seeing every class of things exactly as it is.
When the authority of the power of darkness has ceased, at the falling away of that condition,
<s>Śiva</s>, friend of the world, reveals the atom's infinite vision and action.

children.text: yānvimocayati svāpe śivāḥ sadyo bhavanti te
children.translated_text: Those whom he releases in sleep immediately become <s>Śivas</s>;
or, at dissolution or at emanation, they become atoms or else lords.
They come to share the stations of <s>Rudra</s>, mantra-lord, and <s>Īśāna</s>.
Those whom he favors during maintenance, taking up a conscious guru,
those embodied beings upon whom power descends even for cessation,

children.text: teṣāṃ talliṅgam autsukyaṃ muktau dveṣo bhavasthitau ||
children.translated_text: for them the sign of that is eagerness for liberation and aversion toward remaining in becoming,
devotion toward devotees of <s>Śiva</s> and faith in the rule taught by him.
By this there is inference of the remaining cause even for those of gross intellect.
For those who have attained the yoga of bound-soul vision, the two manifestations of karma are equal,
when they are fit for the results beginning with the highest, in liberations that still have authority.
Because of distinctions in respect for the means, that triad is again sought out.
Some factor manifests the two and is marked by falling away and attainment.
But when there is slight cessation of purpose, in the obstructing function of the lord of darkness,
these signs arise in embodied beings when a little residue remains.
Having passed beyond even this threefold fitness, <s>Maheśvara</s>
favors the atom in sleep, since this state has authority.
At the root of creation, in the third condition, at the dissolution of beings as in sleep,

children.text: sa yad vyapāsya kriyate tadvidho yo 'ṇur ucyate ||
children.translated_text: the atom is called one of that kind according to what is set aside and what is done to it.

children.text: tathā bījaṃ śarīrādeḥ pācayaty ā niveśanāt
children.translated_text: Likewise he ripens the seed of the body and the rest until entry,
though it has not taken on fitness as a constituent; it would be immediate, like medicines and the like.
Even when it is fit for ripening, it is not able to ripen itself by itself.
This is just the common property of everything that undergoes transformation.
He is omniscient because he is the maker of all, together with the means, auxiliaries, and results.

children.text: yo yaj jānāti kurute sa tadeveti susthitam ||
children.translated_text: That whatever one knows, one does, and that one is exactly that, is well established.
And because this knowledge of his is free from covering, it does not depend on a revealer.

children.text: tan na sāṃśayikaṃ tasmādviparītaṃ na jātucit ||
children.translated_text: Therefore it is not doubtful, nor is it ever the opposite.
Things that look to a revealer because they are covered by the powers of impurity,
may even be contradicted in accordance with their revealer.

children.text: nādhyakṣaṃ nāpi tallaiṅgaṃ na śābdamapi śāṃkaram
children.translated_text: The pure knowledge of <s>Śaṅkara</s> does not appear as perception, nor as inference from a sign,
nor even as verbal testimony, but always with respect to all objects.
That one knowledge, because its objects are infinite, assumes infinite differentiation.
Agency, because it is not different from that, is likewise spoken of figuratively.
Those who know the reality of the Lord through slight indications of existence, own-form, instrument, purpose, command, and vision,

children.text: te mocayanti bhavino bhavapaṅkamagnān no vistareṇa puruṣāḥ paśupāśarūpam ||
children.translated_text: liberate beings sunk in the mud of becoming, without extensively discussing the form of soul, bond, and bondage.
Now the definition of the self, the occasioning cause of the universe, has been reached.
It has mostly already been covered in the statement about the Lord, yet a brief indication is given.
The effect, earth and the rest, has the Lord as maker; it is not of use to its maker.
Nor is it for its own sake, because it is insentient; nor is it purposeless, because that would burden the agent.
By elimination, therefore, it is for the sake of another; that other is the <s>kṣetrajña</s>, distinct from those two.
Since the body is for his sake, earth and the others too are surely for another's sake.
The body too, because it is unconscious, is all the more admitted to exist for another.
If it were conscious, this would never be so, because it is an object of enjoyment and because it changes.
Objects of enjoyment that undergo change, such as cloths and the like, are seen to be devoid of consciousness.

children.text: yasminsati ca sattvādvā na satyapi śave citiḥ ||
children.translated_text: And when that is present there is consciousness because of sentience; even in a corpse, though the body exists, consciousness is not present.
If memory exists because of the particularity of transformation, then it is not so;
nor, in this way, since it is very well established, is there anything in the body other than the rememberer.

children.text: nāvyāpako na kṣaṇiko naiko nāpi jaḍātmakaḥ
children.translated_text: He is not non-pervasive, not momentary, not single in the sense of being inert by nature,
nor is he a non-agent; joined with distinct consciousness, at the end of the bonds he is taught to have the state of <s>Śiva</s>.
Now the bonds, beginning with ignorance, are described briefly,
on whose disappearance the atomic souls become lords of the world.
If there were no bond, on what basis would dependence have to be explained?
If it were natural, then among the liberated the word 'liberated' would cease to apply.
Mastery is seen in one free from bondage, and subjection in one who is bound;
this much is the boundness and liberatedness of the bound and the liberated, according to you.
That dependence would be boundness; if it were eternal in him, like consciousness and the rest,
the whole assemblage of means to liberation would be useless. Enough of this notion.
Although he is a treasure of eternal, pervasive consciousness-power, for the accomplishment of an object

children.text: pāśavaṃ śāmbhavaṃ vāpi nānviṣyaty anyathā balam ||
children.translated_text: he would not seek either animal or divine power, if it were otherwise.
That covering of this atomic soul, in the five-streamed teaching of <s>Śaṃkara</s>,
has always been sung under many synonyms, though unseen by bound souls:
by terms such as animality, animal state, frost, death, stupor, impurity, collyrium,
ignorance, covering, disease, weariness, sin-root, and night, and the like.
That one thing, beginningless, dense, and great, belongs to all beings,
like a group of powers abiding in each self and disappearing at its own time.
If it were beginninglessly present there, or later, and if that were its cause, or otherwise than that,
and it also obstructed the liberated, then effort toward liberation would be false.

children.text: tadekaṃ bahusaṃkhyaṃ tu tādṛg utpattimad yataḥ
children.translated_text: That one thing is, however, numerous in count, since such a thing has origination;
rather, its powers are many, because simultaneous liberation is not observed.
Among those powers, the power of <s>Maheśvara</s>, auspicious and gracious to all,
is figuratively called a bond only because it follows their properties.
It transforms these powers up to obstruction with the radiance of a saw-like consciousness;
when it brings about opening, then it is called gracious.
If what is to be graced by <s>Śambhu</s>, namely consciousness and the rest, is mutually opposed to it,

children.text: yugapan na kṣamaṃ śaktiḥ sarvānugrāhikā katham ||
children.translated_text: and cannot occur simultaneously, how is the power gracious to all?
How, for the Lord of the world who acts for the benefit of beings,
is it proper to enter what is harmful and to strike and pierce?
He does not bestow grace upon the impurity of the atomic soul in order to pierce it;
rather, whatever is done is done by means of that, and not otherwise.
No one attains liberation while darkness still has authority;
and authority too ceases through the transformation of that power.

children.text: so 'pi na svata eva syādapi yogyasya vastunaḥ
children.translated_text: That too would not occur by itself, even in a thing that is fit,
because the unconscious is in every way and always set in motion by consciousness.

children.text: yathā kṣārādinā vaidyastudann api na rogiṇam
children.translated_text: Just as a physician, even while piercing a patient with alkali and the like,
is understood at the end to be a cause of pain because he grants the desired result,
so, because <s>Maheśa</s> is all-pervading, the substratum is not destroyed,

children.text: na ca yatrāsti kartavyaṃ tasminn audāsyam eti saḥ ||
children.translated_text: and where something is to be done, he does not become indifferent toward it.
Grace toward a possessor of properties is what is called the following of those properties;

children.text: na so 'sti kasyacij jātu yaḥ patyā nānuvartyate ||
children.translated_text: there is never anyone who is not so followed by the Lord.
The grace of the bound soul whose frost-like power has lost its authority increases when it exists,
and for another it exists because action is directed to that purpose.
It is the following of the two properties, being a knower and being subject to transformation,
when impurity, while still possessing authority, ceases through falling away from that.

children.text: ityevaṃ yaugapadyena kramāt sughaṭa eva hi
children.translated_text: Thus, both simultaneously and successively, this is indeed quite coherent;
and the same has been stated for māyā while it still has authority, and for karma.
Now, from the senses, the body, and objects, a cause of the connection with consciousness is inferred,
because they are future effects; for what is not future does not have such a cause.
Because it exists in a region, because of its variety, because it is momentary,
because it is fixed for each person, and because it is continuous, it has that as its property.
Because it depends on the Lord, knowledge, and the like, it is called a co-operating cause;
karma is unseen because it is produced by activity and because it is subtle in nature.
It produces, sustains, and is to be experienced, serving the triad beginning with the internal self;
because it is the source of truth and untruth, it has the nature of dharma and adharma.

children.text: svāpe vipākam abhyeti tat sṛṣṭāv upayujyate
children.translated_text: In sleep it comes to fruition; in creation it is employed;

children.text: māyāyā vartate cānte nābhuktaṃ layameti ca ||
children.translated_text: it persists at the end of māyā as well, and what has not been experienced does not go to dissolution.
Thus karma, beginningless and setting in motion māyā and the rest up to time,
is also a manifester; when it is immediately obstructive, it is not for liberation.
Now, on the basis of the word of the omniscient one, the mark of the knot-like bond that has been accepted
is also described to some extent, briefly, by reasoning.

children.text: tad ekam aśivaṃ bījaṃ jagataś citraśaktimat
children.translated_text: That one inauspicious seed of the world, endowed with varied powers,
obstructive until the end of the authority of its auxiliaries, is pervasive and imperishable.
By the very reason, namely the property of the world, through which an agent is inferred,

children.text: tenopādānam apyasti na paṭas tantubhir vinā ||
children.translated_text: a material cause also exists; there is no cloth without threads.
That must be unconscious, because unconsciousness is observed in the effect;
otherwise the fault that removes everything would follow, namely the absence of rule among causes.

children.text: yadyanityam idaṃ kāryaṃ kasmād utpadyate punaḥ
children.translated_text: If this effect is impermanent, from what does it arise again?

children.text: avyāpi cet kutas tat syāt sarveṣāṃ sarvatomukham ||
children.translated_text: If it is non-pervasive, whence would that be, facing everywhere for all beings?

children.text: yad anekam acit tat tu dṛṣṭam utpattidharmakam
children.translated_text: What is multiple and unconscious is seen to possess the property of origination;

children.text: na tad utpattimat tasmād ekam abhyupagamyatām ||
children.translated_text: but that is not originated; therefore one thing should be accepted.
A cloth is seen to arise from a mass of threads; everything is one from multiplicity,
and that multiplicity too is produced from one seed alone.
For those who hold that even the unconscious arises from a cause whose nature is consciousness,

children.text: teṣāṃ dhūmena liṅgena jalaṃ kiṃ nānumīyate ||
children.translated_text: why should water not be inferred from smoke as the sign?
For those for whom the world extends as far as the elements and whose cause is atoms,
the subtlety of knowledge itself is already known from the reason stated before.
If body and the rest come from body and the rest, when all of that has completely perished,

children.text: kā vārttā nākhiladhvaṃso na sarvajño mṛṣā vadet ||
children.translated_text: what account can there be? If there is not the destruction of all, the omniscient one would speak falsely.

children.text: ekadeśe'pi yo dharmaḥ pratīto yasya dharmiṇaḥ
children.translated_text: When even in one part a property is apprehended in some bearer of that property,

children.text: sa tasya sarvataḥ kena jāyamāno nivāryate ||
children.translated_text: by what can it be prevented from arising for that bearer everywhere?
Having seen the death, by the tens of millions, of embodied beings that are compounds,
that time too is recognized in which there is the destruction of every creature without remainder.
At dissolution, effects, having those as their supports, function in the form of powers;
at expansion, in the form of manifestations, they operate for the accomplishment of their objects.
If, when there is no cloth, one seeking cloth takes up causes such as threads,
while, when it exists, even the word "cause" disappears, then the world is ruined.
Let there be usefulness for causal things in the arising of what does not exist;
then let everything produce from everything whatever is desired.

children.text: athāśakyaṃ yataḥ śakyam atra vaḥ kiṃ niyāmakam
children.translated_text: If, however, what is possible arises from what is capable, what here is your regulator?

children.text: naca paśyāmi tatkiṃcit śaktiś cet siddhasādhyatā ||
children.translated_text: And I do not see any such thing. If it is power, then what is to be proved is already established.
Otherwise, because the activity of the whole collection of causes would be unintelligible,

children.text: śrutir ādānam arthaś ca vyapaitītyapi taddhatam ||
children.translated_text: scripture, taking up, and purpose would also disappear; therefore that too is defeated.
If there is a productive power, but the effect is not in the form of power,

children.text: tayor viśeṣaṇaṃ vācyaṃ naitat paśyāmi kiṃcana ||
children.translated_text: the distinction between the two must be stated; I do not see any such thing.
Therefore the generative power of a causal thing is what regulates what is produced;
it is ascertained by positive and negative concomitance, or by established usage.
Its manifestation is called generation, because it depends upon its causes;
therefore the cloth-form, which is contained in the threads, is obstructed by other forms.
Then, when it is uncovered by the loom and the like, the manifestation of the cloth is revealed,
just as cloth and the like, hidden by mats and the like, are revealed when those are removed.

children.text: nāsataḥ kriyate vyaktiḥ kalāder granthitas tathā ||
children.translated_text: The manifestation of a non-existent thing is not produced; so too the <s>kalā</s> and the others are bound by knots.
Born of the knot are <s>kalā</s>, <s>kāla</s>, <s>vidyā</s>, <s>rāga</s>, the human soul, and the mothers,
then the guṇas, intellect, ego, mind, senses, subtle elements, and gross elements, in order.

children.text: vidhatte dehasiddhyarthaṃ yat sākṣād yat padāntarāt
children.translated_text: What each directly accomplishes for the attainment of a body, and what through another station,

children.text: yathā yunakti yaddhetos tādṛk tad adhunocyate ||
children.translated_text: and in what way it joins, and for what reason: that is now stated just as it is.
The agentive power of the atom is eternal and all-pervasive, like the power of the Lord;
but, because it is covered by darkness and lacks grace, it does not shine forth with regard to objects.
<s>Hara</s>, having stirred <s>māyā</s>, creates the assisting principle called <s>kalā</s>, luminous in nature;

children.text: māyāṃ vikṣobhya kurute pravṛttyaṅgaṃ paraṃ hi tat ||
children.translated_text: for that is the supreme limb of activity.
By that, resembling a lamp, for the atom whose consciousness is not clear,
he reveals one part, cutting through the dense darkness.

children.text: kala ityeṣa yo dhātuḥ saṃkhyāne preraṇe ca saḥ
children.translated_text: The verbal root <s>kal</s>, as in the word <s>kala</s>, has the senses of counting and impelling;

children.text: protsāraṇaṃ preraṇaṃ sā kurvatī tamasaḥ kalā ||
children.translated_text: because it performs both expulsion and impelling of darkness, it is <s>kalā</s>.
Thus these two together, O <s>vipra</s>, standing as if inseparable,
they have called the agent-cause for the creature in the procedure of enjoyment and action.
Thus, when the power of action has become manifest, the soul wishes to see the field of vision,
but, unable to see by itself, it requires grace.
For that purpose the Lord, having stirred <s>kalā</s> itself, which is capable of producing,
created the principle called <s>vidyā</s>, the instrument of the supreme self.
By that, whose form is illumination and which makes the power of knowledge shine forth,
it knows the supreme object to be accomplished by all the causes.
Even though the object has been seen through that manifested power of consciousness, it is still not thirsty for it;
therefore the Lord created <s>rāga</s>, which generates that desire.

children.text: sa tena rañjito bhogyaṃ malīmasamapi spṛhan
children.translated_text: Colored by that, longing for the enjoyable even though it is impure,
it takes it up, and even while enjoying it does not attain dispassion.
Thus set in motion by instruments established as effects and provided with worlds,
the man enjoys time-governed enjoyments in the realms of enjoyment.
<s>Kāla</s>, time, born from <s>māyā</s>, is the object of cognitions such as a moment and the rest;
measuring, from rising up onward, the bound soul fixed by <s>niyati</s>.
Some have said that karma is the regulator of enjoyment together with its means,
because karma governs, and because what is other than it is excluded.
Enjoyment is the purpose of all the principles, and it too is bound to karma;
so let body and the rest be karma itself; then everything else is useless.
But if it depends on body and the rest and accomplishes the purpose of the person,
then let karma, dependent on <s>niyati</s>, be the regulator.
From that very source arose the principle of the person, the basis of the cognition "person,"
which completes <s>pradhāna</s> and the rest and, in the worlds, rests in <s>Rudra</s>.
Then from the <s>kalā</s>-principle he generated the principle belonging to <s>pradhāna</s>,
which is the cause of the secondary one, the source of the seven knots.
From that come the secondary material cause of intellect and the rest: sattva, rajas, and tamas.
Their functions, illumination and the like, are for the most part well known.
Although the three guṇas are such, that principle is one because they are inseparable from it;
the hearing of each one separately is based on the predominance of its function.
There is no insentient thing in this world

children.text: yanna vyāptaṃ guṇair yasminneko vāmiśrako guṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: that is not pervaded by the guṇas, and in which one unmixed guṇa exists.
From that comes the principle of intellect, characterized by cognitions of many states,
the highest object of enjoyment for the self, refined by the matter to be explained.
The states that are qualities of intellect are <s>dharma</s>, knowledge, dispassion, and powers;
these are sāttvika, while by reversal, except for desire, they are tāmasa.
The cognitions whose material cause is that are famous in groups: eight, nine, fourfold,

children.text: sapta pañca ca vikhyātāḥ siddhyādyā vargaśo mune ||
children.translated_text: seven, and five, O sage, beginning with accomplishment and the rest.
The states are accompanied by their corresponding cognitions; their characteristics are stated from a small part.
For the atom they are innate, acquired through discipline, and natural.
For those whose minds have been kindled by the conditioning of exceptional qualities and <s>dharma</s>,
an innate quality shines forth as before, even in the absence of a body.
An acquired quality shines forth from worldly understanding, teacher, and scripture.
The acquired quality is accumulated by the activity of mind, speech, and body.
The natural quality becomes manifest in connection with a body, like cognition in dream and the like.
Heaven, liberation, the non-obstruction of being material nature, passage into a womb, descent into hell, and bondage
arise in order, with obstruction, among the objects belonging to disciplinary and natural forms.
Subjugation, taking possession, conjunction with knowledge of that, unwillingness toward enjoyments, and the disappearance of a mass of obstacles,

children.text: bhogāsaktir nyakkṛtir dehalabdhir vighnaś cārthāsteṣu sāṃsiddhikeṣu ||
children.translated_text: attachment to enjoyments, humiliation, obtaining a body, and obstruction: these are the objects among those innate qualities.
Now the general definition of the groups beginning with accomplishment is stated in brief,

children.text: kathyate viplavo mā bhūt samāsokteḥ prabhedaśaḥ ||
children.translated_text: so that there may be no confusion, since the summary statement is according to divisions.

children.text: puṃsprakṛtyādiviṣayā buddhir yā siddhir atra sā
children.translated_text: Here, the cognition whose objects are <s>puruṣa</s>, <s>prakṛti</s>, and the rest is <s>siddhi</s> (accomplishment).

children.text: tuṣṭir nur akṛtārthasya kṛtārtho 'smīti yā matiḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Tuṣṭi</s> is the thought of one who has not fulfilled his aim, namely, "I have fulfilled my aim."
<s>Aśakti</s> is inability with respect to a real object when the operative cause is absent.
A cognition elsewhere, with respect to something only in a general way, is another thing, namely <s>viparyaya</s> (error).
Because it illuminates, <s>siddhi</s> is born from the state of <s>sattva</s>, concerning the manifest and so on.
And because it proceeds for the sake of illumination, it is also produced from a portion of <s>rajas</s>.
Because <s>tuṣṭi</s> has a false nature, it is grounded in the quality of <s>tamas</s>.
Yet because it has the form of pleasure, O <s>Brahman</s>, it is also determined to be sāttvika.
Because <s>aśakti</s> does not proceed, it is tāmasī; because it has the nature of pain,
a rājasa quality is also seen in it, for the effect depends on the cause.
<s>Viparyaya</s> has <s>tamas</s> as its source, since it has a false form;
and because it appears as mere generality, it is ascertained to have <s>sattva</s> as its self.
Thus this illumination of intellect, characterized by state-cognitions,
is called <s>bodha</s> (cognition), because it is the ground for the manifestation of cognition in the bound soul.
If intellect is the cause of cognition, then <s>vidyā</s> would be superfluous apart from it.
And when true dispassion exists, what does <s>rāga</s>, the source of <s>kalā</s>, accomplish?
If, when another revealer exists, a revealer is useless,
then, when mind, deity, and object exist, intellect too is without purpose.
Now, some say this with reference to its being an instrument;
but that position too is remembered as inconclusive, because the gods have mind as their sixth.
If, when there is a single application, one thing is exceeded,
then let hearing, sight, hands, feet, and the rest have different purposes from that.
And there is in no way a single application for <s>vidyā</s> and intellect.
Through another mode of application, a plurality of things to be accomplished is not faulty.
<s>Vidyā</s>, the manifest power of consciousness of the atom, having impelled the objects of the senses, the lord of the senses, and the senses,
and having taken them up, comes to be the object of the instrument employed by the person.
Cognition is different from that; <s>rāga</s> is not secondary, because it has a nature contrary to it.
And either that enjoyability or this is destroyed by the dispassionate person; therefore that objection is defeated.
<s>Rāga</s> is the desire for objects, and it does not exist in the two kinds of object.
But karma should be conceived as pervasive, since even when it is conceived there is the other case.
The objection to karma alone has been stated only with regard to <s>niyati</s>.
The fault is that they cannot coexist, not that hatred and attachment are dissimilar.
Every activity of everyone at all times arises from the cognition of pleasure.
For one who has acted, pleasure, pain, or delusion then arises.
After activity comes hatred; attachment belongs to the time before that.
After hatred, by means of that again, it becomes the cause of powerful conjunction.
Now, from another manifest principle, ego arose as the instrument of consciousness.
From its operation the five bodily winds set themselves in motion.
They, beginning with <s>prāṇa</s> and <s>apāna</s>, are different in function, not in reality.
As I explain their function briefly, O <s>Bharadvāja</s>, listen to me.
The function called leading forth is what is called life.
That deliberation, the thought of human beings, wanders like a blind person seeking the path.
Performing that, it is called <s>prāṇa</s>; or it is <s>prāṇa</s> because of its connection with breathing.
The word <s>prāṇa</s> is also used for the power that carries consciousness beyond, and among the <s>kalās</s>.
Likewise, when it carries away what has been eaten and drunk, feces, urine, and semen,
it is sung by the knowers of reality under the name <s>apāna</s>.
When it evenly distributes food and drink all around, with equalization,
it is called <s>samāna</s>; <s>vyāna</s> is so called from the bending of the body.
By the prior effort of the wish to speak, from the sound that is a quality of the space in the belly,
by the help of the organ of speech, phonemic form is produced by that.
That is <s>udāna</s> in this body. The place of each, its sustaining,
its conquest as a result, and the remaining matter to be stated have been taught by the Lord in another section.

children.text: atha śeṣārthasiddhyarthaṃ skandhān asyāta eva saḥ
children.translated_text: Now, for the accomplishment of the remaining topic, from this very one
he drew out its three sections, predominated by <s>sattva</s> and the rest, and directed by the Lord's power.
They are remembered as <s>taijasa</s>, <s>vaikṛta</s>, and the other, called <s>bhūtādi</s>.
From them come the gods together with the subtle elements, and from the subtle elements the five gross elements.

children.text: śrotraṃ tvakcakṣuṣī jihvā nāsā ca manasā saha
children.translated_text: Hearing, touch, the two eyes, the tongue, and the nose, together with mind,
are sāttvika because of their connection with illumination; and the <s>taijasa</s> too is sāttvika.

children.text: vāṇī pāṇī bhagaḥ pāyuḥ pādau ceti rajobhuvaḥ
children.translated_text: Speech, the two hands, the organ of generation, the anus, and the two feet are born of <s>rajas</s>.
Because of their connection with action, the group here that is <s>vaikārika</s> is predominated by <s>rajas</s>.

children.text: śabdaḥ sparśaśca rūpaṃ ca raso gandhaśca pañcamaḥ
children.translated_text: Sound, touch, form, taste, and smell as the fifth
are the subtle elements, undifferentiated as qualities and designated by the term <s>tanmātra</s>.
Because they differ from the class that produces illuminating action, they arise from <s>tamas</s>.
And because it is something to be illuminated, <s>bhūtādi</s>, among the forms of <s>ahaṅkāra</s>, is tāmasa.
Mind is what sets the deities in motion, moves swiftly, and has the nature of conception;
with respect to objects such as sound and the rest, the graspers are hearing and the other senses.
Speech, taking, enjoyment, emission, and movement are the actions
of speech and the others; although their place exists, they are not endowed with that quality.
When self, sense, and object are not in proximity, all the deities fail to operate;
therefore the existence of something that causes activity is ascertained even by reasoning.
Because it is distinct from the functions stated for the other principles, conception is a distinct thing;
it becomes the seed, and mind is established as that by elimination of what remains.
Cognition, since it is connected with that sense-organ, is connected in sequence and therefore occurs successively;
yet it appears simultaneous, because there is no lack of rapid movement.
For someone, the sense-organs have determinate objects and diverse sources of origin;
and because they manifest smell and the other objects, they also have the nature of their supports.
The ear grasps sound alone, and the skin grasps touch alone;
let that be so, if it does not take up another cause endowed with qualities.
The skin-sense grasps an object not in conjunction with it and turns away from what is conjoined;
the eye takes up fiery, watery, and earthy substance together with its form.
Therefore it would be produced from three substances; but this is not accepted by another view.
Whatever object is perceived by a given thing, that thing is the cause of that object.
Even action and the rest, though present, are not obtained: this is a chain of troubles.
Space qualified by the aperture of the ear illuminates the class of sounds.
Tell, then: what prevents that same space, qualified by the aperture of the nose?
Or if it is obstructed by unseen force, what has that force done elsewhere?

children.text: prāptaṃ gṛhṇāti nātodye śaptaṃ kenāpi dasyunā
children.translated_text: It grasps what has come into contact, but not in a musical instrument, as if cursed by some bandit.
Even where reasoning cannot reach, cognition from a true statement is free from obstruction.
The wise say that what has unlimited scope is superior to what has limited scope.
Space, wind, fire, water, and earth are the five <s>bhūtas</s> (elements),
having qualities beginning with sound, each with one more than the preceding, and possessing functions such as providing room.
